text: Copilot Automations can now learn from their outcomes and propose improvements to themselves, helping them produce better results over time. It’s easy to create an automation, but harder to build one you can trust to consistently produce high-quality results. Reviewing its output and improving its prompt by hand takes time. Self-improvement uses feedback from real outcomes on GitHub to make that process easier. Your automations leave a trail of signals on GitHub that show how well they’re working. For example: Self-improving automations use these signals to propose improvements to their prompts. You stay in control: each proposed change comes to you for review before it’s applied. When you ask Copilot to set up a self-improving automation, it can create a group of automations that work together. You can review and accept or reject the proposed change before it is applied. To learn more, see about Copilot Automations . Copilot Automations is available with Copilot Pro, Pro+, Max, Business, and Enterprise plans. Join the discussion within GitHub Community .
